steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **Schedule the tasks** in *Topological sort*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: Kahn's algorithm on six tasks. What does it print?
code: for (var v = 0; v < n; v++) graph[v] = new List<int>();
foreach (var e in edges) { graph[e[0]].Add(e[1]); indegree[e[1]]++; }
for (var v = 0; v < n; v++) if (indegree[v] == 0) queue.Enqueue(v);
steps.explain: 4 and 5 start free. Removing 4 leaves 0 and 1 still waiting; removing 5 frees 2 and then 0. 2 frees 3, and 3 finally frees 1.
hints: Start: in-degrees are 0:2, 1:2, 2:1, 3:1, 4:0, 5:0, so the queue begins as 4, 5.
